request.deadline: 12 months; pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027
deliverables: WP 1: Community-Facing Technical Coordination, including technical expert event attendance and commissioned technical reports.
WP 2: Protocol Governance and Evolution, funding the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group.
WP 3: Technical Review, establishing a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027.
Full expenditure accounting with return of any unspent funds to the Cardano treasury.
Use of Intersect treasury management smart contract tooling with external oversight and dashboard tracking.
request.recipient: Intersect, submitted on behalf of the vendor, with funds directed to the 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Intersect Technical Steering Committee Support activities for 12 months, including community engagement, protocol governance, and independent technical review.

claims.claim: Intersect requests 1,193,000 ADA, stated as $298,250, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The budget is allocated as 256,000 ADA for WP 1, 832,000 ADA for WP 2, and 105,000 ADA for WP 3.
The proposal states that all expenditure will be fully accounted for and any unspent funds returned to the Cardano treasury.
Execution of the work packages is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting and audit documentation.
The proposer claims the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
Independent audits and assurance for the proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews of deliverables, controls, spend validation, and milestone evidence.

The Technical Steering Committee has not received Cardano Treasury funding in the past 24 months, while Intersect and its committees have received 22,385,000 ADA through listed prior governance actions.
The proposal claims the Technical Review work package will improve DRep decision-making by providing independent technical evaluations of core infrastructure proposals.
Intersect will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts, with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based approvals, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard for auditability.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of Intersect TSC support across three work packages, gives a high-level budget split, names governance and smart-contract oversight mechanisms, and references external voting, audit, and contract materials, but the deterministic assessment identifies missing complete summary, budget analysis, feasibility, risk, alternatives, and failure-mode analysis.
